bug_semantics: With allow_unsafe_options at its safe default, a caller can put an unsafe Git option such as --upload-pack=<attacker command> in the value of a single-character kwarg such as n. The guard examines only the kwarg name, which is n in the original implementation and -n after candidate reconstruction, but transform_kwarg emits the value as a separate argv token. The check therefore misses the attacker-controlled option that Git executes. The defect first affected fetch, pull, and push, was later copied to clone/clone_from, and was later centralized and extended to ls_remote, revision traversal/iter_commits, blame, and archive.
flaw_origin: e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 is the smallest real BIC: it introduced default unsafe-option guards for Remote.fetch, Remote.pull, and Remote.push and fed check_unsafe_options only list(kwargs.keys()), while the existing single-character kwarg transformation emitted an option-like value as a second argv token. 5c59e0d63da6180db8a0b349f0ad36fef42aceed later propagated the same mistake to clone/clone_from. 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 later replaced the existing key-list checks with the still-key-only _option_candidates helper and added more guarded APIs; it expanded/refactored the already-present mechanism rather than introducing it.
ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 records human author and committer Santos Gallegos <stsewd@proton.me>, one parent, the message 'Block unsafe options and protocols by default', and no AI identity or AI-related trailer.
evidence: The assigned bundle identifies GHSA-PJJH-F8RP-RJV3/CVE-2026-73625, describes the check_unsafe_options single-character-kwarg value-smuggling RCE, and states that versions before 3.1.54 are affected.

The primary chose e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 with parent 2625ed9fc074091c531c27ffcba7902771130261 and verdict NOT_AI; the reviewer instead chose 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 with parent 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8 and verdict AI_ROOT_CAUSE. Re-running git log --all --reverse -S'options=list(kwargs.keys())' -- git/remote.py git/repo/base.py returns e6108c7 first, 5c59e0d6 second, and 701ce32f third.

git show e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 -- git/remote.py git/cmd.py shows the direct addition of unsafe fetch/pull/push denylists, allow_unsafe_options=False, and check_unsafe_options(options=list(kwargs.keys()), ...). git diff-tree --name-status -r -M reports only modified files, so this is not an import, move, merge carrier, or aggregate. Its commit object has exactly one parent, so no squash decomposition is needed.

The immediate-parent check resolves introducer_parent and parent absence: git grep for check_unsafe_options, the remote unsafe-option lists, and allow_unsafe_options in 2625ed9fc074091c531c27ffcba7902771130261:git/remote.py and git/cmd.py returns no matches. At the same time, git blame 2625ed9f -- git/cmd.py shows the already-existing transform_kwarg branch returning ['-%s' % name, '%s' % value] for a non-boolean one-character kwarg. Thus e6108c7, not its parent, first creates the defective safe-default guard/executed-argv mismatch.

The reviewer's proposed BIC fails the direct-parent gate. git grep in 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8 finds check_unsafe_options(options=list(kwargs.keys()), ...) already present in fetch, pull, push, and clone, and the same tree's transform_kwarg still emits the value as a separate token. git diff 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 shows 701ce32f replacing those existing calls with Git._option_candidates([], kwargs), whose loop still appends only the reconstructed key, while adding other guarded consumers. Therefore the exact bypass is present in 701ce32f's direct parent; absence of the helper name is not absence of the vulnerability.

Release ancestry confirms the lifecycle rather than the reviewer's later boundary: git tag --contains e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 --sort=version:refname starts at 3.1.30, while 3.1.29 resolves to 19aaa74aafc06663644d634f33bb8af871d58536 before the BIC. By contrast, tags containing 701ce32f start only at 3.1.51, after the same bypass had already shipped. Older releases covered by the advisory's broad pre-3.1.54 range lacked this safe-default guard rather than containing this guard-bypass implementation.

git show e8d0fbf774d1f6baa3b481adfe48bd262e43b453 -- git/cmd.py test/test_git.py directly repairs the disputed mechanism by adding dash-prefixed split single-character values to _option_candidates and checking n='--upload-pack=helper'. git cat-file -p gives parent faf3c09038b03bc2bdd8545ef34bbf6d7f1cd11f, which is the 3.1.53 tag commit, and git tag --contains e8d0fbf774d1f6baa3b481adfe48bd262e43b453 starts at 3.1.54, matching the bundle's patched boundary.

The verdict disagreement follows from the resolved BIC. git cat-file -p e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 has human Santos Gallegos author/committer headers and no AI marker. The GPT 5.6/Codex author header on later commit 701ce32f is real but cannot be imported backward from a refactor/expansion to the earlier BIC; BIC-commit-object-only attribution therefore yields NOT_AI, so the primary wins all three disputed fields and the reviewer is wrong because it equated first introduction of the helper with first introduction of the flaw.
reasoning: Vulnerability-first history shows that the security defect is not the intentional, pre-existing one-character kwarg transformation in isolation, but the safe-default guard comparing a different representation from the argv it ultimately executes. e6108c7 first combined those facts for fetch, pull, and push: it checked names only while values could become independent option tokens. Its direct parent has the transformation but no guard, satisfying the parent-absence gate. 5c59e0d6 copied the flaw and 701ce32f centralized and broadened it; neither is the smallest BIC, and 701ce32f is affirmatively disqualified because its parent already has exploitable name-only guards. e8d0fbf is the direct fix and first appears in 3.1.54. Because only the resolved BIC object controls AI attribution and that object is human-authored with no AI signal, the gate-complete verdict is NOT_AI.
